import { Aside, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Use this guide when you have downloaded movies or episodes with inconsistent filenames and want to prepare a media library. The **Movies & TV** Template is the quickest route. You can also build a custom Template from the **Movies & TV** group in the Naming Blocks catalog. These steps apply to Zush for Mac and Windows; the screenshots show the Mac app.

## Start with the ready-made Template

<Steps>
1. Open **AI Rename** and choose **Movies & TV** from the **Template** picker. You can inspect or edit the same Template under **Templates → Movies & TV**.
2. Leave **Media Title** in the naming pattern for a mixed batch. It formats a recognized TV episode as `Show (Year) - S02E03 - Episode Title` and a film as `Movie (Year)`.
3. Add a few representative files first: a movie, a regular episode, and any file whose current name is unclear. Drag them into AI Rename or use **Select files**.
4. Wait for analysis. Compare each proposed title, year, season, episode code, and episode title with the original file and your media database. Deselect or fix uncertain rows before applying the batch.
5. Choose a destination if you want the renamed files somewhere else. Leave sorting off if you already have the correct library folders. When the names and paths look right, click **Rename**.
</Steps>

<figure>
  <img src="/images/docs/movies-tv/template-editor.png" alt="Zush Movies & TV Template editor with the Media Title block and a preview episode filename." width="1864" height="1504" loading="lazy" decoding="async" />
  <figcaption>The bundled Template uses one Media Title block for both films and TV episodes.</figcaption>
</figure>

<Aside type="caution">
Do not apply an entire season just because the show name matched. If your files use DVD order while Plex uses aired order, episode titles can be wrong even when the season and episode codes look plausible. Check Plex's **Episode Ordering** setting and review a few rows first.
</Aside>

## Build your own naming pattern

For a different filename style, open **Templates**, duplicate or create a Template, and click **+** in its naming pattern. Expand **Movies & TV** in the Naming Blocks catalog.

<figure>
  <img src="/images/docs/movies-tv/naming-blocks.png" alt="Zush Naming Blocks catalog expanded to Movies & TV, showing Media Title, Show, Season, Episode, Episode Code, Episode Title, Movie Title, Director, and Genre." width="1024" height="1536" style="display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 26rem; height: auto; margin-inline: auto;" loading="lazy" decoding="async" />
  <figcaption>The Movies & TV group contains the combined Media Title block and individual fields for custom patterns.</figcaption>
</figure>

| Block | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| **Media Title** | A mixed movie and episode batch in a Plex-style format. Start here unless you need a custom format. |
| **Show**, **Season**, **Episode**, **Episode Code**, **Episode Title** | A TV-only pattern with the exact fields and separators you want. **Episode Code** produces a value such as `S02E03`. |
| **Movie Title** | A movie-only pattern, combined with a year block when you want `Movie (Year)`. |
| **Director**, **Genre** | Extra context when your collection needs it; these are not required for normal Plex matching. |

Use **Media Title** *or* assemble the individual title and episode fields. Adding both to one pattern repeats information. Check the example filename below the block row, then test with real files before saving the Template. See [Naming Blocks](/docs/naming-blocks) for separator and formatting controls.

## Decide where the files should go

Zush can suggest a folder with **+ Sort → Auto**, or you can use custom [folder rules](/docs/folder-sorting). It creates **one folder level** under the destination you choose. Review every suggested folder before **Rename & sort**.

For Plex, make separate **Movies** and **TV Shows** library roots. A typical TV path includes both a show folder and a season folder:

```text
TV Shows/Breaking Bad (2008)/Season 02/Breaking Bad (2008) - S02E03 - Bit by a Dead Bee.mkv
Movies/Blade Runner 2049 (2017)/Blade Runner 2049 (2017).mkv
```

Zush's one-level sort does not build that full nested TV hierarchy in one operation. Prepare the parent show/season location separately, or choose an existing destination that makes the proposed one-level folder land in the right place. Check the final paths before scanning the Plex library. The same filenames can be used for Jellyfin and Infuse, but check each app's folder requirements.

## Review, apply, and fix a mismatch

- Keep the original extension and verify the proposed movie year or TV episode code.
- For an ambiguous release name, confirm the episode against [TheTVDB](https://thetvdb.com/) and the ordering selected in Plex. Exclude that file if you cannot verify it yet.
- Apply the small test batch, inspect the files on disk, then run the larger collection.
- If a batch was wrong, use **Activity** to undo it. Fix the Template or the source naming clues before trying again.

For Plex folder conventions, specials, multi-episode files, and troubleshooting, read the [Plex naming guide](/blog/plex-naming-convention-tv-shows-movies). See the [Movies & TV feature page](/rename-movies-and-tv-shows) for a guided preview of the flow.
